# Vendored third-party trees

Plain-tree vendored copies (not submodules). **Never edit vendored code** —
portability/build issues are handled from the top-level CMakeLists (target
scoping, options, the pkg-config shim), not by patching. To update, re-copy a
newer tree and update the provenance below.

| tree | upstream | vendored commit | copied from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devourer/` | https://github.com/OpenIPC/devourer | `30d248e` (#409–#424) | Plain-tree copy of upstream `master`; `reference/` and `.gitmodules` excluded. No local vendor delta. This includes the upstreamed RTL8822E MCS4+/48M+ TX, `0x41e8` RX-desense, eFEM/DPDT, calibration/runtime, and channel-switch fixes from `b5a6df7` (#238/#268), superseding the former `snokvist/devourer` cherry-pick pin; the per-unit EFUSE MAC identity (`IRtlDevice::GetPermanentMacAddress`, #383/#386) and the Jaguar3 EFUSE-walk append-order fix (#384 — flips 8822C `rfe_type` 0→3, a 7-RF-register delta; CU bench re-baselined, see `docs/findings.md` 2026-08-07); the RTL8733BU monitor RX / raw TX backend (#388) and its `FastRetune` port (#398, 345→55 ms per hop). The `5bf059a` bump adds the **RTL8733BU §10.5 TX-power actuator** (#399) — `GetTxPowerCaps().supported` flips false→true on that family, which is all `io/src/air_radio.cpp`'s `power_actuator_ok` reads, so the §10.5 announce and the §10.6/§10.7 calibration refusal self-enable with no consumer change. The `d2120b4` bump adds the **RTL8733BU USB TX aggregation port** (#400, merged as `52c6549`) — `send_packets` packs up to 3 `[txdesc][frame]` blocks per bulk-OUT URB, which is what `air.usb_tx_agg` + `RadioAir::inject_staged` exist to drive. Unlike the `5bf059a` bump this one is **not** self-enabling: `cfg.tx.usb_agg_max` defaults to 0 and the per-frame path stays byte-identical until a profile opts in. It also picks up **#401** (`d2120b4`), the maintainer's follow-up from #400's review: `bulk_send_sync_ep` returns *bytes submitted*, so `rc >= 0` also matched a short write, and Jaguar2/Jaguar3 counted those as delivered on BOTH their single-frame and aggregated paths. Both now require a full write, matching the 8733B and Kestrel. That reaches us: on 8812CU/EU `send_packet` now returns false where it returned true, which is what `RadioAir::inject` already treats as not-sent — strictly better accounting, and unreachable in practice besides (`UsbTransport::tx_sync` returns negative on every libusb error including timeout, so `0 <= rc < len` needs libusb to report success on a partial bulk-OUT). The 8733B's own delta is log-only: a hard transport failure now reaches stderr instead of only a short write. This row previously pinned #400's PR head; issue #215 owned the re-pin and is closed by it. The `f86f92d` bump adds the **RTL8733BU hardware-ARQ surface** (#406, #407) and its narrowband qualification (#403), plus RF characterization that is tests/docs only (#402, #404, #408). Three caps flip false→true on that family alone: `ack_responder_ok`, `tx_retry_limit_ok` and `narrowband_ok`, and `bw_mask_for_generation` gains `kBw10` (5 MHz is explicitly refused — that die's BB small-BW mode airs no packets). Like #399 and unlike #400 these are read by code we already ship, but the only consumer is a **refusal** that now stops firing: `air_radio.cpp`'s §3.0 Pass 156 leg rejects `return.unicast` on a TX die with `tx_retry_limit_ok=false`, so an 8733BU elected as the uplink can now carry unicast returns where it previously refused to start. Nothing self-arms — `air.ack_responder` still defaults off. The contract change reaching the fleet dies is `SetAckResponder` on Jaguar1/2/3: it now rejects a non-unicast MAC and **propagates the write's transport status** (`ack::enable` became `bool`), returning false where it used to `return true` unconditionally, and `ClearAckResponder` uses `disable_verified`. It is **not** a register readback — only the 8733B calls `ack::verify()`; upstream deliberately declines it on the Jaguar dies until each has a bench cell, since a family whose `0x0102` does not read back would start refusing healthy arms. The unicast gate can never fire against us: `kWbSaPrefix0` is `0x56` (`io/include/wblink/dot11.h:53`) and byte 0 is constant across net_id/originator/tx_idx, so `(mac[0] & 1) == 0` always. The status leg does reach us — `air_radio.cpp:529` treats false as the §3.0 loud-degrade leg and latches `ack_supported=false`, which `air_radio.cpp:310` documents as one-way — so a single transient control-write failure (500 ms `USB_TIMEOUT`) now reports the responder unsupported for the rest of the session on a craft that arms it, and `deploy/vehicle-192.168.2.232.json:89` is exactly that craft. The direction is honest (the old path reported a silently dead responder as armed) but the permanence is new. Against that, the bump **removes two uncaught-abort paths** the same craft was exposed to: old `ack::enable`/`disable` read `0x0102` through `ctrl_read`, which throws `std::ios_base::failure`, and both were `void` and unguarded, so a failed control read escaped `SetAckResponder` -> `arm_ack_responder` -> `RadioAir::create` with nothing catching it; both are `noexcept` with `catch(...)` now. #406 also makes devourer's own init throw when a configured `rx.ack_responder` cannot be armed; waybeam-link never sets that DeviceConfig field (it calls `SetAckResponder` directly after bring-up) and `DEVOURER_ACK_RESPONDER` is parsed only in an example TU that is never linked, so that path is unreachable from here. One NEW throw *is* reachable: `src/rtl8733b/Rtl8733bDevice.cpp:109` aborts bring-up when the `REG_ACKTO`/`REG_ACKTO_CCK` readback does not match the requested window, and we set `dc.tx.ack_timeout_us` on every adapter (`air_radio.cpp:1267`), so it runs on every 8733BU bring-up in the `x86-ground`, `rk3566` and `cv610` builds and is not caught around `InitWrite`. It joins seven throws already in that function, so the escape class is pre-existing rather than introduced here; device-verified latching on both fleet 8733BU units (a ground and the CV610 craft, each streaming >20 min on this pin). Optional Kestrel 11ax and non-fleet Jaguar families are forced off by the top-level CMake; waybeam-link builds 8812AU/CU/EU and RTL8733BU (`WBLINK_DEVOURER_CHIPS`) and enables only the devourer features it explicitly configures. The `30d248e` bump is the first that is **downstream-breaking by design**, and it carries three RX/ACK changes that reach adapters we already fly. **The contract split (#415).** `IRtlDevice` becomes `IRadio` (`src/IRadio.h`), `WiFiDriver::CreateRtlDevice` becomes `CreateRadio`, and `devourer::IRtlTransport` becomes `devourer::ITransport` (`src/Transport.h`); the five members whose meaning is fixed by Realtek silicon move to a new `IRtlRadio : IRadio`. Upstream deliberately shipped **no `using` alias and no forwarder**, so this is a compile break, not a deprecation. Ported at four sites in `io/src/air_radio.cpp` (`:21` include, `:182` member, `:1305` factory call, `:2056` reference) — the factory signature is unchanged. **Every one of the ~23 devourer methods we call is on `IRadio`; none is `IRtlRadio`-only**, so there is no downcast and no shim, and `air_radio.cpp` never needs to know which family it holds. That is the property that makes a non-Realtek backend possible for us at all. `third_party/devourer/src` was already our include dir, so no build wiring moved. **PHY-status parsing is now gated on the descriptor PHYST bit (#409)** on Jaguar1/2/3 — all three of our fleet families. `REG_RX_DRVINFO_SZ` is global, so drvinfo space is reserved on *every* frame while the PHY writes a report only where DW0 bit 26 is set; the old size-only gate therefore parsed stale bytes on all-but-one subframe of an A-MPDU and folded them into the RF running averages. For us the reachable surface is per-frame `RxAtrib.rssi/snr/evm`, which `air_radio.cpp:691` folds into the §15.3 quality window. Three guards absorb an unfilled frame: `rssi_dbm_from_chains()` returns the previous value rather than zero, the accumulator skips `rssi_raw <= 0` itself, and — new in this bump — it skips a zero SNR too (`if (snr_raw != 0)`, RxQuality.h). **That retires the §15.3 asymmetry**, which pinned EVM as presence-guarded and SNR as not; an earlier draft of this row argued the #409 risk from the old asymmetry and was wrong about the tree it was describing. The real per-frame residue is subtler: `snr_mean_raw`'s denominator moved from every frame to SNR-bearing frames only, so any die mixing reporting and non-reporting frames publishes a HIGHER mean across this bump, undocumented upstream. On HT-only wblink traffic every frame reports and the two denominators coincide, so nothing we ship moves — but a family that does not report SNR now yields `snr_valid=false` (also new at 30d248e) rather than a zero mean, and a consumer that ignores that flag republishes 'no measurement' as '0 dB'. In practice we should never see a PHYST-clear frame: the link transmits per-frame broadcast injection, and `air.usb_tx_agg` is USB bulk packing, **not** 802.11 A-MPDU, so each frame is its own PPDU. Device-checked rather than assumed — see the measurement note below. `GetRxQuality()` itself is read only by `rx_sense()`, the energy sweep, which already degrades to a sensor-less path. **A live ACK disarm now moves the identity (#410 for 8733B, #411 for Jaguar1).** On the reference RTL8812AU the old gate-only `ClearAckResponder()` read back successfully while the port kept sending SIFS ACKs for the armed MAC — 1120/1120 soliciting frames still ACKed after a "successful" clear. Jaguar1 now snapshots port-0 MACID/BSSID before the first arm and readback-verifies a restore on clear and on failed-arm rollback. This is a straight fix for any craft or ground running `air.ack_responder`. #411 also **rejects a responder equal to the captured MACID**; that can never fire against us, because we arm a wblink SA whose byte 0 is the constant `kWbSaPrefix0 = 0x56` (`io/include/wblink/dot11.h:53`), never the adapter's factory MAC. **FCS presence became a per-frame fact (#420).** `rx_pkt_attrib::fcs_present`, defaulted true, with no Realtek parser touched — every Realtek generation sets the MAC's append-FCS bit at init, so it was a no-op for us **only while no MT7612U was built**. It exists because the MT7612U MAC strips the FCS and the four bytes after the MPDU are an FCE info trailer instead (CRC-32 matched 0 of 4263 measured frames), so a consumer that blindly trims four bytes there deletes payload. We were that consumer: `mpdu_len_without_fcs()` subtracted `kFcsLen` unconditionally, so the moment the ground presets enabled the family every MT7612U frame reached `dot11_parse` four bytes short. The headers are at the FRONT, so originator/net_id still resolved and the frame was neither filtered nor dropped — `rx`, `rssi`, `snr` and the MCS histogram all advanced normally — and only `decode_data`'s length-exact check rejected it, as `kLengthMismatch`, which has no counter anywhere. Two MT7612U ears reported the best SNR on the node and contributed zero packets, with `diversity` pinned at 0. `fcs_present` is now a REQUIRED argument of that helper (`io/include/wblink/radio_decode.h`) so the assumption cannot be reacquired by omission. Treat every `fcs_present`-shaped field in a future bump the same way: a vendored tree that turns one of our constants into a per-frame fact breaks nothing at compile time. **The MT7612U backend itself (#412, #414, #421–#424) is present in the tree but not built.** `DEVOURER_MT7612U` defaults OFF upstream (`third_party/devourer/CMakeLists.txt:57`) and this change does not set it, so every preset compiles exactly the families it did before — deliberately, so that a regression on a Realtek ear belongs unambiguously to the four changes above and not to a new family. Enabling it for the ground presets is a separate change. **This bump raises the Android NDK floor to r27, and that is the one thing a downstream consumer must act on.** #410 (RTL8733B) and #411 (Jaguar1) introduced `std::jthread` / `std::stop_token`. NDK 26.3's libc++ ships **no `<stop_token>` header at all**, so r26 cannot build the vendored tree by any flag; `WBLINK_ANDROID_NDK_PIN` moves to `27.3.13750724` accordingly. r27 alone is still not enough — libc++ treats both as *incomplete* features and `__config` defines `_LIBCPP_HAS_NO_EXPERIMENTAL_STOP_TOKEN` unless `_LIBCPP_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL` is set, so `<thread>` declares no `jthread` whatever the `-std=` level. The top-level CMake therefore adds `-fexperimental-library` to the devourer target under `if(ANDROID)` — target-scoped and from our own CMakeLists, never a patch to the vendored tree. **Waybeam-android is exposed sooner than our own bionic gate is**: `:wifi` builds `WBLINK_DEVOURER_CHIPS=all`, which compiles the RTL8733B backend #410 touched, while the gate's default `fleet` excludes it — so the app hits this on r26 the moment it bumps its devourer pin, and needs both the NDK move and the flag. Reported upstream; devourer declares `cxx_std_20` but `std::jthread` is not portably available at that level on libc++. |
| `libusb-cmake/` | https://github.com/libusb/libusb-cmake | `c8477c1` (includes the `libusb/` sources) | same Android checkout |
| `nlohmann/` | https://github.com/nlohmann/json | 3.12.0 single-header | (io layer only — core stays zero-dep) |

Build integration (top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, `WBLINK_RADIO=ON`):
- libusb is built static from `libusb-cmake` (examples/tests off, udev off —
  we never hotplug; the SSC338Q cross toolchain has no libudev).
- devourer's `pkg_check_modules(libusb-1.0)` is satisfied by
  `cmake/pkgconf-libusb.sh` (answers only libusb-1.0: cflags → the vendored
  headers, libs → empty); the real static target `usb-1.0` is linked directly,
  devourer before usb-1.0 (static archive order).
- Chip options match the fleet exactly, selected by `WBLINK_DEVOURER_CHIPS`:
  `fleet` (default) = JAGUAR1 (8812AU) + JAGUAR3_8822C (8812CU) +
  JAGUAR3_8822E (8812EU); `au` / `eu` / `8733b` pin one family for a craft
  build; `all` adds RTL8733BU **and the MediaTek MT7612U** to the fleet trio
  for a ground that may meet any craft. MT7612U is reachable only from `all`,
  so it is compiled for `x86-ground` and `rk3566` and for nothing else — no
  craft carries one, and it is the only non-Realtek family in the tree.
  8814/Jaguar2/Kestrel/PCIe are off in every combination, and the top-level
  CMake **fails** if the vendored tree builds a family that was not asked
  for — MT7612U included, which is what keeps it out of the craft images.
